items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity is high for fleet-wide go-live, new public exposure, and security-sensitive releases; ordinary reversible growth may continue conditionally when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence: security fleet-doctor is not OK and has no run, checks, findings, or site results; operations has no deploy, uptime, or error-sweep results; and authentication/access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS configuration, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are unevidenced. Compliance is technical-only at 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown, not certification. Recommendation: preserve existing private-launch and security-sensitive release gates; do not claim clearance or certification; continue only authorized read-only evidence work.

Security gate: do not admit security-sensitive releases or new public exposure until dated evidence exists for access boundaries, secrets, isolation, release/deploy controls, dependencies and supply chain, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, and disclosure readiness. Existing reversible work may proceed only if it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior and passes normal review, validation, rollback, and compliance checks.

items.title: Maintain evidence-needed fleet security disposition and release gates
items.summary: Fleet-wide security clearance is unsupported because the security fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results and material security controls remain unevidenced. Preserve private-launch and security-sensitive release gates while allowing constrained ordinary reversible growth.
items.requested_action: Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record timestamps, affected scope, owners, severity, exact unknowns, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, and security.txt or disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, deploy, add dependencies, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
